title: Job 40
paragraphs: ¹ The LORD said to Job: ² "Will the one who argues with the Almighty correct him? Let the one who accuses God give him an answer." ³ Then Job replied to the LORD: ⁴ "I am unworthy — how can I reply to you? I put my hand over my mouth. ⁵ I spoke once, but I have no answer; twice, but I will say no more."

⁶ Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind: ⁷ "Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will answer me. ⁸ Would you discredit my justice? Would you condemn me to justify yourself? ⁹ Do you have an arm like God's? Can your voice thunder like his? ¹⁰ Then adorn yourself with glory and splendor; clothe yourself with honor and majesty.

¹¹ Unleash the fury of your wrath; look at all who are proud and bring them low. ¹² Look at all who are proud and humble them; crush the wicked where they stand. ¹³ Bury them all in the dust together; shroud their faces in the grave. ¹⁴ Then I myself will admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

¹⁶ Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you — it feeds on grass like an ox. ¹⁷ What power it has in its loins, what strength in the muscles of its belly! ¹⁸ Its tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of its thighs are tightly knit. ¹⁹ Its bones are like beams of bronze; its limbs like rods of iron. ²⁰ It is the chief of God's works; yet its Maker can approach it with his sword.

²¹ It lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds in the marsh. ²² The lotuses conceal it in their shadow; the poplars along the stream surround it. ²³ When the river rages, it is not alarmed; it remains calm though the Jordan rushes against its mouth. ²⁴ Can anyone capture it by the eyes, or trap it and pierce its nose?
